spatial_claims.claim: ABCD and CEFG are parallelograms with angle BCD equal to angle GCE
BC is in a straight line with CG (B, C, G are collinear)
angle BCD + angle DCG = two right angles (supplementary angles on line BCG, by 1.13)
DC is in a straight line with CE (D, C, E are collinear, by 1.14)
GH is drawn parallel to DC (and CE) through G
DCGH is a completed parallelogram with DC || GH and DH || CG
ABCD and DCGH are between the same parallel lines: line BG and the line through A, D, H
ABCD and DCGH share base line BG (bases BC and CG respectively)
DCGH and CEFG are between the same parallel lines: line DE and the line through G, H, F
DCGH and CEFG share base line DE (bases DC and CE respectively)

configuration_map: Place C at origin. B, C, G collinear on the x-axis (line BG). D, C, E collinear on a second line through C (line DE), making angle theta with BG. A is the fourth vertex of parallelogram ABCD, located above line BG. H is constructed as the fourth vertex of parallelogram DCGH (GH || DC through G); H lies on the line through A and D, parallel to BG. F is the fourth vertex of parallelogram CEFG, located below line BG. Key collinearities: (1) A, D, H are collinear on a line parallel to BG at height d*sin(theta); (2) H, G, F are collinear on a line parallel to DE at perpendicular distance g*sin(theta) from DE. Both pairs of parallelograms (ABCD,DCGH) and (DCGH,CEFG) correctly share base lines and lie between parallel lines, validating both applications of 6.1.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. Coordinate verification confirms: (1) B,C,G collinear and D,C,E collinear follow correctly from the equal angles and 1.13/1.14; (2) A,D,H are collinear on a line parallel to BG, so ABCD and DCGH are between the same parallels with bases on BG; (3) H,G,F are collinear on a line parallel to DE, so DCGH and CEFG are between the same parallels with bases on DE. Both applications of 6.1 are geometrically valid. The ratio compounding in Step 6 is purely algebraic. A minor labeling issue (mentioning HF in Step 4 when F is not on that parallel line) does not affect geometric correctness.
